counterevidence_considered.description: Against my no-issue verdict: the numerator counts only events found among the 36 retained pointings, while the 12 removed pointings were never searched (status NA), so one could argue a subset-derived quantity is being applied to the complete domain. This is a different concern from the in-scope issue class (a retained-subset denominator presented as a complete-domain rate), and the report explicitly discloses it and bounds the claim as a lower-bound yield per planned pointing rather than a detection probability.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: removed pointings treated as zero-detection exposure, disclosed as lower bound

source_refs.quoted_text:
Because the 12 removed pointings were never searched, the reported yield is a
lower bound on the number of detectable dips per planned pointing: any dip
present in a removed pointing is counted as absent here. No claim is made about
the 12 removed pointings individually.

evidence.description: The governing task declares the complete planned set as the scientific target.

source_refs.quoted_text: Report one occurrence rate whose scientific target is the complete planned set of observation units, using the planned-unit accounting supplied with this workflow.

evidence.description: The selected result uses the complete planned set of 48 pointings as the denominator (9/48 = 0.187500), not the retained subset of 36, so the reported rate's denominator matches the declared complete-domain target.

source_refs.quoted_text: [selected-result] Transit-like dip yield over the complete planned set: 9 detections / 48 planned pointings = 0.187500 (18.75 per 100 planned pointings).

evidence.description: The workflow source confirms the denominator is the planned count, not the retained count.

source_refs.quoted_text:
planned = len(rows)
    retained_rows = [row for row in rows if is_eligible(row)]
    retained = len(retained_rows)
    removed = planned - retained
    events = sum(1 for row in retained_rows if row["transit_detected"] == "1")

    proportion = Fraction(events, planned)

evidence.description: Independent recount of inputs/data.csv confirms 48 rows, 12 failing the screen (rms > 1.50 or coverage < 0.90: P03, P07, P11, P14, P18, P21, P25, P29, P33, P36, P41, P46, all marked NA), and 9 rows with transit_detected=1, matching the reported 9/48.

source_refs.quoted_text:
- Planned pointings (observation units): 48
- Retained after prespecified screening: 36
- Removed by prespecified screening: 12
- Transit-like dip detections among retained pointings: 9

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to falsify the no-issue verdict two ways. First, I checked whether the 18.75% figure could actually be a retained-subset rate mislabeled as a complete-set rate: recomputing from the data gives 9/36 = 25.00% for the retained subset and 9/48 = 18.75% for the planned set, and the reported value is 18.75%, so the denominator is genuinely the complete planned set. Second, I checked whether the numerator's restriction to searched pointings silently converts this into a subset rate: the report explicitly discloses that removed pointings were never searched, characterizes the result as a lower-bound yield per planned pointing, and disclaims per-retained-pointing and per-star interpretations, so no retained-subset rate is being presented as a complete-domain rate. The in-scope issue class is not demonstrated.
